_how_to_edit: Replace these placeholder people with your own family and friends.
Every suspect needs a name, a sex (male or female) and a value for every trait.
No two people may have the same sex AND the same crime computer traits, or the computer can't tell them apart.
Values work best as short words that several people share: two people with black hair, two who get around by bicycle, and so on. The crime computer lists them as written.
Each trait's clues are witness sentences; {value} becomes that person's value. In sentences, {They}/{they}, {Them}/{them} and {Their}/{their} become he/him/his or she/her/her.
phrases (optional) say how witnesses word a value when it doesn't read well on its own: the computer shows Bald, a witness says he had no hair at all.

computer: false marks a trait the crime computer doesn't have. Other is one: witnesses may mention it, and it shows in the dossier, but it can't go on a warrant. Write it to follow 'he' or 'she', like 'collects stamps'.
catchphrase (optional) is what they say when you catch them. bio (optional) shows as Notes in their dossier.

skin is optional too: light, rosy, olive, tan, brown or dark, for the drawn portrait of anyone without a photo in assets/suspects/. The rest of that portrait (hair, beard, glasses) comes from the words in their traits.

traits.label: Hobby
clues: {They} asked if there was anywhere nearby for {value}.
{They} said {they} never missed a weekend of {value}.

traits.label: Vehicle
clues: {They} said nothing beats getting around by {value}.
How did {they} get here? By {value}, {they} said.

traits.label: Other
clues: I'll tell you one more thing: {they} {value}.
